title: Selected upper bound of a finite set
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set in the sense of [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] (any two elements have a common upper bound). Fix a base point $i_\varnothing\in I$; for each pair $(i,j)\in I\times I$ a selected common upper bound $d(i,j)\in I$, so that $i\leq d(i,j)$ and $j\leq d(i,j)$ (one exists by directedness); and an auxiliary linear order $\prec$ on the underlying set of $I$, unrelated to $\leq$ (one exists by the well-ordering theorem). For a finite subset $F\subseteq I$, list its elements in $\prec$-increasing order $i_1\prec i_2\prec\cdots\prec i_n$ and define

$$
u(\varnothing)=i_\varnothing,
\qquad
u(F)=d\bigl(\cdots d\bigl(d(i_\varnothing,i_1),i_2\bigr)\cdots,i_n\bigr).
$$

Equivalently, $u(F\cup\{i\})=d(u(F),i)$ whenever $i\notin F$ and $j\prec i$ for every $j\in F$. Since the enumeration of $F$ is fixed by $\prec$, $u$ is a well-defined function on finite subsets of $I$ and does not depend on an order of insertion (without such a fixed enumeration the insertion recursion is not well defined, since $d$ need not be commutative or associative). The property $i\leq u(F)$ for $i\in F$ is not part of this definition; it is proved separately by induction on $F$, adjoining the $\prec$-largest element.
